# Which update caused Helldivers 2's negative reviews to spike between August and October 2026, and what exactly are players complaining about?

The negative review spike in October 2026 was caused by the "Devoid of Liberty: 7.2.0" update released on 2026-10-20 [R54]. This update introduced Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC), the Scope of Authority Warbond, and various weapon and stratagem rebalances [R54]. The addition of EAC led to a severe review spike, resulting in 6754 negative reviews and 3813 positive reviews (63.9% negative sentiment) during the 2026-10-01 period [R33]. Players are complaining that EAC causes constant crashes, prevents the game from launching entirely, breaks cosmetic and other mods, and is unnecessary for a PvE cooperative game [R62][R69][R71].

---

### Timeline

* **2026-06**: The game had 25423 average concurrent players, peaking at 45817 [R35].
* **2026-07**: Average concurrent players rose to 26750 with a peak of 43782 [R36].
* **2026-08-06**: An official announcement detailed plans to raise the level cap from 150 to 300 [R40].
* **2026-08-12**: The major "Devoid of Liberty: 7.0.0" update launched, introducing a new biome and Illuminate enemies [R41][R42].
* **2026-08-17**: Patch 7.0.1 fixed crashes related to full-screen terminals and superwide windows [R43].
* **2026-08-25**: Patch 7.0.2 addressed crashes in the Vehicle Customization menu and Dynamic Resolution Scaling [R45]. Player counts for the 2026-08 period averaged 52422 concurrent players with a peak of 144799 [R37].
* **2026-09-22**: Patch "Devoid of Liberty: 7.1.0" introduced community feedback changes, such as preventing enemies from targeting unoccupied vehicles [R48]. Player counts for the 2026-09 period dropped to 45156 average concurrent players with a peak of 92006 [R38].
* **2026-10-20**: The "Devoid of Liberty: 7.2.0" update launched, introducing Easy Anti-Cheat, the Scope of Authority Warbond, and bug bile enemy adjustments [R54].
* **2026-10-22**: Patch 7.2.2 (listed as 7.2.1 in notes) released to resolve squad joining and leaving crashes [R55].
* **2026-10-29**: Patch 7.2.2 updated the AMW-20 APEX and LAS-44 NOVA stratagems to fix armor penetration and demolition strength issues [R56].
* **2026-10**: Player counts for the 2026-10 period decreased to 39956 average concurrent players with a peak of 98111 [R39], while negative reviews spiked to 6754 [R33].

---

### What players are complaining about

The main player complaints target the introduction of Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) [R62][R71]. Reviewers highlight several core issues:

* **Launch Failures and Errors**: Many players are completely unable to launch the game, experiencing persistent issues like the "0x0000142" error or "0xc0000142" error [R71][R79][R84].
* **Broken and Softlocked Mods**: The anti-cheat softlocked all mods, including cosmetic mods, forcing the game to crash or close [R69][R72][R74]. Purging mods does not always restore game functionality [R69].
* **Restrictive Measures**: Players express frustration over a restrictive anti-cheat in a cooperative PvE game, noting that it even blocks players from changing process priority in Task Manager [R62][R73].
* **Performance and Developer Disconnect**: Reviews report a severe drop in performance and optimization [R78]. Players also cite unaddressed bugs like stratagem bouncing [R63], impossible Major Orders, and poor rewards [R78], criticizing a disconnect between developer vision and player desires [R65][R72].

The following reviews illustrate player frustration with the update [R62][R69][R71]:

> "They changed the Anti-Cheat (on a PvE game??) to EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat) which not only, likely broke some mods, has the potential to ban players from a false-positive, but many players cannot even launch the game anymore." (228.7 hours played) [R62]

> "Great until they softlocked anyone running mods, even cosmetic mods cause the anticheat to force close my game. After I purged all the mods, game still wouldn't run, ArrowHead needs to cut easy anticheat." (211.2 hours played) [R69]

> "Easy Anti-Cheat literally has made me unable to play the game at all. I've done every single way posted to fix this 0x0000142 Error. now I'm unable to play one of my favorite games." (135.7 hours played) [R71]

---

### What the data can't answer

* **Console Impact**: Since the average and peak concurrent player counts and review totals are from Steam, the data cannot show if PlayStation 5 players faced similar issues, though some players enjoy the game across both PS5 and PC [R33][R35][R65].
* **Error Distribution**: The data cannot show the exact ratio of players who cannot launch the game versus those who can play but object to the anti-cheat's presence [R62][R71].
* **Developer Intentions**: The data does not explain why developers chose to implement Easy Anti-Cheat beyond what is stated in the 2026-10-20 announcement [R54].
* **Reviewer Representation**: Steam reviews only reflect players who write reviews, which may not represent the entire active player base [R33].
* **Owner Estimates**: SteamSpy owner counts are only estimates, and no console player counts or console review data are available to compare against Steam [R33][R35][R39].

HELLDIVERS 2 Is Raising the Level Cap to 300

Attention, Helldivers. Super Earth has authorized a new tier of service, and it's a big one: the level cap is jumping from 150 all the way to 300.

If you are already sore from the democratic path to 150, take a breath before you panic, this update comes with some genuinely great news for anyone who's already put in the hours.

A Quick History of the Cap

- 
Launch cap: Level 50
[/*]
- 
April 2024: Tripled to level 150
[/*]
- 
Now: Doubling again to level 300
[/*]

Each time the cap has risen, it's been paired with new titles, ranks, and bragging rights for the players who've stuck around–from our veterans of Malevelon Creek, to our soldiers in the Battle for Super Earth, to those brave divers who held the Menkent Line and beyond. This time is no different; level 300 is arriving as part of a broader progression overhaul that also brings Galactic War Campaigns and Personal Campaign Progression tracks, giving you new rewarding goals to chase even when the wider community's Major Order doesn't pan out.

The Numbers

Let's be honest about what we're looking at here:

- 
Reaching level 150 already takes many, many hours of dedicated sessions… Several hundreds of missions across dozens of Galactic War campaigns.
[/*]
- 
Reaching level 300 will take more than double that. This isn't a small bump; it's a genuine second act for anyone chasing the next rank.
[/*]

If you're not already at the cap, don't stress about "falling behind." All the weapons, stratagems, and gear that actually matter for your loadout unlock by around level 25. Everything past that is about demonstrating your veteran prestige and prowess in battle. Level 300 is a marathon–not a sprint–designed to let you continue to demonstrate to your fellow Helldivers your skill and commitment to fighting for Super Earth.

The Best Part: Your XP Is Already Banked

Here's the part worth getting excited about. If you hit level 150 before this patch drops and kept playing anyway, none of that XP was wasted.

The game has saved every drop of experience you earned over 150; even past the current cap. The moment the new limit goes live, the game recalculates your total XP against the new level table and instantly bumps you up to wherever you should be. No re-grinding, no starting over. Just an immediate jump that reflects the missions you’ve already completed with your fellow divers, the battles you’ve already won, and the contributions you’ve already made to the ongoing war.

This is exactly what happened the last time the cap rose from 50 to 150: players who'd kept farming missions past level 50 logged in and found themselves instantly promoted several levels, sometimes dozens, based purely on banked XP. Expect the same behavior this time around.

So if you've been running Super Helldive missions "for nothing" since hitting 150, surprise, you've actually been quietly stacking up levels 151, 152, 153, and beyond. You just haven't seen the number tick over yet.

What This Means Going Forward

- 
New veteran players (already at 150): Log in after the patch and watch your level jump based on banked XP. Keep playing normally in the meantime, every dive counts💪.
[/*]
- 
Players still working toward 150: No change to your path. Keep pushing toward the current cap; the new ceiling will be waiting for you.
[/*]

Expect new titles and ranks to fill out the stretch between 150 and 300, giving long-term players fresh milestones (and hopefully some fresh bragging rights) all the way to the new ceiling.

For Super Earth, for glory, and for that sweet, sweet liberty! See you on the battlefield, Helldivers.

I'm your host, Release Captain Morris. When humanity is at stake, we bring you this update from Super Earth High Command to further your efforts in the war.

*** INCOMING TRANSMISSION FROM SUPER EARTH HIGH COMMAND ***

Helldivers, you are needed on the battlefield of a new frontier–one more wild and uncertain than any we have faced prior. We are so close to entering the Void.

Stay frosty, divers. As you fight your way toward the Void, you’ll encounter new, hideously mutated organisms. We have received intelligence reports that indicate these metamorphosed creatures are emerging from the heart of the Void–they are ghoulish diversions wrought into existence by the Illuminate scourge to threaten our freedom. 

We aren’t sending you in without backup. You may now gain all 300 ranks of security access and privileges, and we have commissioned SEAF platoons to aid you on the surface of the Void source planet.

This is our opportunity to strike and avenge the citizens, SEAF, and Helldivers lost in the Battle for Super Earth.

This is our chance to destroy them.

📍 Patch Highlights

New Illuminate Enemies

A new biome full of fresh horrors awaits, the void warps everything it touches and your foes have taken new hideous forms.

- 
The Crusher is on a deathmarch capable of regenerating while taking heavy damage and needs to be worn down quickly and consistently without a moment of pause.
[/*]
- 
The Wretch is a relentless and nimble enemy that requires quick trigger fingers and focused aim as they are able to dodge and leap at the player while advancing to quickly dismantle its weapons along with their will to live.
[/*]

SEAF Support 

SEAF have entered the battle! 

Super Earth Armed Forces (SEAF) can now appear as a planet modifier, joining you in battle in your missions and enhancing your combat capabilities with a range of new tools (Stim pistols, Heavy Machine guns and more)

- 
The SEAF take to the stars. Super Earth High Command has mandated the SEAF be deployed directly to the frontlines of the Galactic Campaign for Democracy. Helldivers will be able to be supported by friendly SEAF NPC troops, with new and improved behavior, weaponry and updated visuals
 
[/*]

Level Cap Increased

We've expanded the Helldiver rank system beyond Level 150, adding 15 new ranks and titles that carry Helldivers all the way up to Level 300. Each new rank comes with its own unique title and icon to recognize the most dedicated defenders of Managed Democracy. Super Earth thanks you for your continued service, the fight never ends, and neither does your potential.

Expanded Emote Slots

Behind the scenes: The Hive Lord

The Origin of the Hive Lord

Hello there! It is I, Niklas Malmborg, Design Director for Helldivers 2.

Let’s talk about our old friend: the Hive Lord! And we can start with what he was back in the first game.

During the development of the original HELLDIVERS, we really liked the idea of a bossfight that was massive and fit the faction. The Terminids are a subterranean species, so a giant tunneling creature fits and has a certain nerdy allure to it for unrelated reasons.

Being an important but so far not overly revealed part of the Terminid societal structure, it comes with a purpose to the Hive Worlds and it might be related to the tunnels the Helldivers “carefully” venture in to. Suggesting such a thing as a structure to Terminids society or even suggesting they have a society is a punishable offence of course. 

The first HELLDIVERS serves as a source of content that players can look forward to because they know it’s a canon part of the universe (like the Bastion, Lumberer, Trident etc). We won't necessarily bring back everything from the first game, but we want to bring back a lot and the Hive Lord was near the top of the list.

Due to technical limitations in the first game we made it as large as we could, but there was an urge to make it bigger and more majestic. Still, the resulting monster hit the emotional targets we were aiming for and players understood the potential scale of the Terminids.

How we Heralded it in HELLDIVERS 2

In HELLDIVERS 2, players have been able to see the bones of the Hive Lord as a beast of the past. We wanted those bones to serve as a promise to eventually show you the beast in its full glory and to be a motivator for us internally of what the game should eventually introduce.

So how did we approach it?

We started with making a list - of everything that the Hive Lord needs to be and have in order to be the biggest, baddest Terminid life form (so far). This is what we decided: 

(some of the text is not perfect sentences, its copy pasted from the working documents)

1. MASSIVE

An impressive scale and cinematic appearance to instill awe and fear.

2. ELUSIVE

Only appears on certain planets, and only sometimes. 

3. BURROWER 

Underground traversal, deforming terrain as it moves and erupts, arcing and diving like a dolphin.

4. GRATUITOUS VIOLENCE 

Simple movement, attack, and death. It’s head/top visible while navigating half-submerged in terrain. A simple-yet-massive acid spray to destroy players. 

5. HARD TO KILL

It has a massive health pool that's reflected physically on its body/segments to show players how much damage they've done.

6. BAIT 

Players can influence Hive Lord behavior using both discreet and explicit tactics. Hive Lord has readable roaming behavior and provides opportunity for bait mastery. 

(Yeah, it detects disturbances of the earth, so you can bait it with explosions, barrages etc. Or it can find you if you’re too noisy in combat. Have fun!)

With our list completed, we prioritized our work and knew that, if we hit all the points, we would have made a truly monstrous Terminid. 

Here are a few of our images of the development and some more specific notes:

Animation:

In the animation files we ended up using Motionbuilder and a Human IK rig for the Hive Lord, meaning his whole body is made up of a human neck, with the head at the end and the rest of the body at the base. In the source files there are therefore tiny tiny human arm and leg joints around the base of the character that never gets exported. 

Sound: 

The sound team also used a chair dragging against the floor as part of building the iconic sound the Hive Lord makes as it erupts. 

Performance and Rendering: 

We had to develop a lot of new tech to make sure this very large enemy didn't impair performance and memory for players so it functions in segments compared to normal enemies where we render and treat them only as one piece!

Movement:

Previously, all of our enemies used a navigation mesh that dictates where they can move, what type of movement is allowed, and where. The Hive Lord is so massive that we needed to make one specifically for him! It also has different logic, like not moving on rocky terrain, and creates its own map of disturbances (from vehicles, explosions, etc.) to choose where to navigate to.

It doesn’t have a bossfight mission? But it had one in HELLDIVERS!

In HELLDIVERS the Hive Lord could only be found in a separate mission focused only on killing the boss. Why isn't it like this in HELLDIVERS 2?

One thing we actually thought didn't work well in the first game was the bossfights. After you played them a handful of times they became very predictable and repetitive - and that didn’t feel right for HELLDIVERS 2 or for the Hive Lord.

Instead, we thought of the Hive Lord like a force of nature, almost invincible. It roams around the map, churning up the land, stalking players, and creating an anticipatory atmosphere. Players get the chance to try to beat the big scary monster, but are not forced to. It’s possible for players to take on this ridiculously powerful boss enemy, but it's no easy task.

I hope you enjoyed this little dive into the development of the Hive Lord, that's it for this week! I will be back in the future to talk about more exciting development stories!

Launching Devoid of Liberty: A Look Back

From the desk of our Creative Director, Mikael Eriksson

Helldivers,

The Void has been pierced and the Illuminate's latest shenanigans have been decisively dealt with! Well done! 

The Devoid of Liberty launch has run its course and history has been written. Before we dive into whatever comes next, I wanted to take a moment and talk about how I personally think this update landed. 

What We Were Going For

I consider Devoid of Liberty to be a ‘vertical slice’ of what we want this game to be every week. Not in terms of new content (we can’t keep up with that), but in terms of fantasy cohesion. The Void’s presence transcended the game: it was felt outside of the SE Destroyer windows and the Galactic War map. It was in what you read in the mission descriptions, what you saw on the battlefield, what you heard in the war reporting, and what you created as a community. The throughline was strong across the game and the community. 

This is the future that we’re aiming for: a future where the Galactic War is this interesting and dynamic every day, and felt inside and out of the game. 

With the Void specifically, we wanted to dive deeper on Illuminate lore. We had already explored the Terminid Hive Worlds and the Automaton Cyborg Factories, so it felt like the logical next step to expand our universe. The Illuminate are all about mystery, exploring the unknown, and being confronted with technology and intentions you can't fully understand. With Heart of Democracy, we had already told the classic invasion story of "Aliens attacking innocent civilians!" This time we wanted to explore more about who they really are and how they work.

We wanted the Void to feel like stepping into an oppressive, alien environment that actively resented your presence. From the haunting environmental audio design to the unsettling visual distortion of the Void flora, every element was built to keep Helldivers on edge.

The new enemy variants earned their teeth. The twisted, razor-limbed human experiments proved once again the Illuminate’s blatant disregard for the sanctity of human life, something Super Earth could never relate to. We also expanded on the Illuminate Fleet system, and grouped all Illuminate enemies into different Fleets, which gives flavour but also adds to the believability and gives you more to consider when choosing loadouts. Going forward, this sort of thing is what we’re considering for all factions. We don’t want a one size fits all loadout for any Faction, you should always need to consider what you’re about to engage with. 

SEAF squadmates are the thing I'm most hyped about in this update. Fighting with a squad that follows commands, reacts to the fight (and occasionally hugs you mid-firefight, for reasons) is something Niklas Malmborg and I have talked about doing for a long time. It’s a war, after all! As we continue to expand the game, we want to both explore tighter, less crowded spaces as well as bigger, more chaotic battlefields, and this was a crucial step in that direction for us. We also wanted to give solo players and understaffed squads a genuine lifeline without breaking the four-Helldiver core experience.

The Warhammer 40,000 ‘Castellan's Creed’ Warbond brought new blood in without diluting the tone. As always, we chose our partners with great care. If done wrong, a crossover could feel like it's wearing Super Earth's uniform without buying into Managed Democracy, and that is something we won’t do. I think we threaded that needle and ended up with a Warbond that's genuinely great while staying true to the original IP, and I was very happy to see positive reactions from the Warhammer fans. You guys are known to be particular about details!

What We’re Still Working On

Launch stability was too patchy (pun intended). We had nasty crashes on fullscreen terminal interaction and issues for players using ultra-wide monitors. An update of this size needed a cleaner landing, and it took us two follow-up patches to get there.

These big beats should run for longer, and the endings should be more clearly shaped by the community. The two things we've heard most since the Devoid of Liberty launch: you wanted more time in the Void, and you wanted the community choices to shape the ending in impactful ways. Both of these are impacted by how we structured the campaigns: how many phases a Campaign runs, how long content stays live, and how much room our Game Masters have to react to the community in interesting ways. That's the part we're working on iterating on for the next big update.

Some quality-of-life asks are still sitting in the backlog. Assist-reloading and backpack icon clarity were great wins, but there's still a long list of smaller frictions behind them, and they're on the board.

Where We Go From Here

I'm happy with this update, and it was as fun as always to follow the developments live, but I know there's still room to improve. The Void isn't finished with us, and neither are we with it. Stability will stay the priority between updates, and the campaign structure work above is the one to watch for going forwards. 

Thank you for your devotion to diving and dying and diving again. Stay frosty, Helldivers.

For Super Earth. For Liberty.

Changing anti-cheat in HELLDIVERS 2

Greetings Helldivers,

Today, we want to talk about an upcoming change to our anti-cheat, answer some questions we have seen arise in the community around modding, and discuss how it may impact you as a player. 

Fairness and honor have always been strong foundations for Helldivers in our fight in the Galactic War. But we have seen for too long that there are some who would bend the rules and definitions of fairness, affecting not only their own games but also the battles of those who play alongside them, affecting pick-up rates, and even going so far as to manipulate the war itself, breaking the unfolding story and dragging down innocent players with it. 

We haven't previously commented on modding, other than to warn that from a technical perspective, we can’t guarantee their safety or usability for players. However, we feel that this change, considering what it affects, is giving us an opportunity to do so.

We know mods are part of the DNA of PC gaming and gaming communities as a whole. In general, we appreciate the creativity behind cosmetic and non-gameplay mods, which players can enjoy without negatively impacting those who play alongside them. Where we need to improve is how we protect players against modifications that create unfair advantages or negatively impact others, which goes beyond software manipulation to tamper with our game. 

As a stepping stone on this journey, we are doing two things:

- 
Implementing additional security measures to crack down on recent cheat mods that have been circulating.
[/*]
- 
Transitioning from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat today, October 20th, with additional security tools in place to enhance its effectiveness and improve game integrity protection.
[/*]

These changes mean that some mods, particularly the types that are affecting the experience of other players, may no longer function. It also means that some non-malicious cosmetic mods may require updates from their individual creators in order to keep working.

We believe these are steps in the right direction, and we want to remain transparent about our decisions and intentions as we continue to improve the integrity and security of the game, to give players a consistent and fair experience, and to strengthen trust with our dedicated community.

As always, we appreciate your continued feedback and support, Helldivers. See you on the battlefield.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Why are you changing from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC)?

A. The implementation of GameGuard for HELLDIVERS 2 wasn't as effective as it could have been, and in the end we decided to take another path with EAC. 

EAC is an industry standard used in over 200 games, and we believe this will be an effective way to protect the Galactic War and will better protect fair gameplay and the integrity of the game. 

For more information about EAC, please visit their official support.

Q. My cosmetic mod stopped working–what do I do?

A. Occasionally, mods will no longer function after an update and modders may need to update their projects to ensure they continue working with our updates and patches.

If you feel EAC or another system is blocking a non-destructive mod or other software, we encourage you to reach out to our official support on Zendesk to let us know.

Q. How can I tell which mods are safe to use?

A. Using mods is done at your own discretion, and so we cannot determine what’s safe vs. unsafe to use.

Q. Does the implementation of EAC in HELLDIVERS 2 impose any new hardware requirements?

A. No, there are no changes in hardware requirements. 

For the minimum required specifications for HELLDIVERS 2, please see our article on Zendesk.

Q. I play HELLDIVERS 2 on Steam Deck / Linux. Will I still be able to play?

A. Yes, you can still play. Steam Deck and Linux compatibility remains unchanged.

I have over 2500 hours across PS5 and PC. I genuinely enjoy Helldivers 2, but I’m increasingly concerned about the direction Arrowhead is taking the game. There seems to be a disconnect between what the developers envision and what the player base actually wants. For years, players have provided feedback on longstanding issues, requested quality-of-life improvements, and suggested features that could help move the game forward, yet many of those concerns continue to go unaddressed.

Arrowhead frequently leans on the idea that they built a milsim, but what they’ve delivered and what players largely experience is a cooperative horde shooter. There’s nothing wrong with having a vision for your game, but refusing to acknowledge what your game has become or what your community wants is a recipe for stagnation.

The developers talk about wanting Helldivers 2 to last ten years, but that ambition requires evolution, not resistance to change. Mod support is a perfect example. While Arrowhead has expressed appreciation for modding, they’ve shown little willingness to embrace it as a legitimate way to extend the game’s lifespan, encourage creativity, and give players more ways to enjoy the experience.

You cannot build a long-term live-service game by continually dismissing player feedback, leaving issues unresolved for years, and resisting opportunities to evolve. I want Helldivers 2 to succeed, but wanting a game to last ten years and actually building one that can are two very different things. At this rate, I question whether it will maintain its player base for another six months.
